newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bill on cigarette ingredients introduced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bill on cigarette ingredients introduced.

text.p: A bill to require tobacco companies to list the ingredients and carcinogens in cigarettes was introduced in Congress Tuesday by anti-smoking advocates.

"This legislation will force the tobacco companies to tell the truth to the American people. Unless Congress forces the tobacco industry's hand, it will never tell its customers what it puts in its products," Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Democrat, said at a news conference.

Lautenberg and other co-sponsors said the bill would also require stronger and larger warning labels on cigarette packs such as "Cigarettes kill." They said cigarettes contain 43 different substances that can cause cancer.

"It is time to fully warn children about what tobacco will do to them. It is time to give adults the information they need but still don't have to enable them to exercise the type of informed consent that the public is afforded for other consumer products," said Representative Martin Meehan, a Massachusetts Democrat.
Current law does not require tobacco companies to list their ingredients.
Meehan said recent disclosures by the Liggett Group that cigarettes were addictive and dangerous broke the industry's code of silence about tobacco.
"It is time to stem the growing carnage of tobacco addiction and to end the industry's embarrassing charade as just another legitimate business enterprise," Meehan said.
Other co-sponsors of the bill included Democratic Sens. Richard Durbin of Illinois, Tom Harkin of Iowa and Paul Wellstone of Minnesota and Representative James Hansen, a Utah Republican.
